design.quote: This prespecified analysis examined efficacy, safety, and tolerability of empagliflozin in subgroups with de novo heart failure (NHF) vs acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).

population.value: Patients hospitalized for heart failure, subgroups with de novo heart failure (NHF) vs acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF)
population.quote: empagliflozin improved clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized for heart failure (HF)

sample_size.quote: stratified by HF status (NHF: n = 175; ADHF: n = 355)

intervention.quote: participants were randomized 1:1 to empagliflozin 10 mg/d or placebo

comparator.quote: participants were randomized 1:1 to empagliflozin 10 mg/d or placebo

follow_up.quote: The primary endpoint was a hierarchical composite of death, worsening HF, or ≥5-point difference in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Total Symptom Score (KCCQ-TSS) change at day 90, assessed using a win ratio.

primary_findings.quote: The win ratio was 1.29 (95% CI: 0.89-1.89) for NHF
primary_findings.outcome: Hierarchical composite of death, worsening HF, or ≥5-point difference in KCCQ-TSS change at day 90 (NHF subgroup)
Hierarchical composite of death, worsening HF, or ≥5-point difference in KCCQ-TSS change at day 90 (ADHF subgroup)

primary_findings.quote: diuretic response, which was greater with empagliflozin in NHF than in ADHF from day 15 (mean difference vs placebo: -5.11 [Q1-Q3: -7.89 to -2.32] vs -0.97 [Q1-Q3: -2.91 to 0.96] kg per mean daily loop diuretic dose, Pinteraction = 0.017)
